title: China says it will work with India on business visas after reports of curbs on Indians
dek: Beijing's foreign ministry neither confirmed nor denied reports that its missions have cut visas for Indians, including business travellers, and stopped its outside application centre.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
China said on Monday it was ready to work with India to make it easier for business people from both countries to get visas, responding to reports that its missions have been issuing fewer visas to Indian nationals, including business visas. A spokesperson for China's foreign ministry gave the response in written replies to questions from reporters in Beijing.

"We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson said. The spokesperson did not confirm or deny a reduction, saying only that "China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations."

## What has been reported

According to reports, Chinese missions have cut the number of visas issued to Indians in recent weeks. Fewer Indian business people received visas to attend this month's China International Import Expo in Shanghai, the reports said. Beijing has also stopped the China Visa Application Centre, the outside agency that collected applications, from accepting them; Chinese missions now handle applications themselves, at a time when demand, especially for business visas, is rising.

Neither government has published figures on the number of visas issued or refused, and China gave no reason for the change. No response from India's Ministry of External Affairs had been reported by Monday evening.

## Background: a thaw running both ways

The two countries have been easing travel since relations were badly damaged by the Galwan Valley clash of June 2020, in which 20 Indian soldiers were killed. India resumed tourist visas for Chinese nationals in July 2025 after a gap of five years, and direct flights, including Beijing–New Delhi, have restarted. In December 2025 India eased business visas for Chinese professionals, a step China's foreign ministry welcomed at the time, and the Chinese embassy in India launched an online visa system for Indian applicants. Indian officials have said the rejection rate for Chinese applicants has fallen to about 7 per cent in recent months, according to reports.

The spokesperson linked Monday's response to the meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping in New Delhi in September, on the sidelines of the BRICS summit. "The most important common understanding they reached is that China and India need to be partners," the spokesperson said, adding that China "stands ready to work with India to improve and grow bilateral relations".

## Why it matters for India

Much of India's trade with China depends on business travel. Indian manufacturers send staff to China to inspect and buy machinery, electronic components, pharmaceutical ingredients and solar equipment, and to attend trade fairs such as the Shanghai expo. Any slowdown in visas falls on Indian firms that depend on those supplies, while India has been easing entry for Chinese technicians that its own factories need.

The visa question comes as other strands of the relationship remain unsettled. Military commanders from the two sides have held two more rounds of talks on the Arunachal Pradesh sector of the Line of Actual Control to avoid clashes before winter, according to reports, and an Indian drone industry body has told the defence ministry that Army units issued 580 purchase tenders naming Chinese drones or parts between 2021 and this month.

## What happens next

China's reply does not set out any specific step. Whether Chinese missions restore the earlier pace of business visas, and whether India raises the issue in its regular talks with Beijing, are the next things to watch.
